title: Hand-drawn sequence diagram: driver app token refresh with a retry loop
persona: Marco, an iOS engineer at a food-delivery company, chasing reports of drivers being logged out mid-shift, sketches the access-token refresh as a sequence diagram before asking an agent to explain what the auth code really does.
topic: how the driver app refreshes an expired token mid-shift
realism: Auth flows are the textbook case for a sequence diagram on a whiteboard: tall boxes for each party, numbered arrows down the page, dashed replies, and a box drawn around the steps that repeat. He corrects himself twice (where /token lives, who sends the new tokens back), which is how people really discover what they don't know about auth.

steps.say: This is the token refresh in the driver app, when the access token expires in the middle of a shift.
Time goes down the page. The app on the left, the gateway next to it.
And the auth thing over here, I keep wanting to call it Auth0 but we moved off that last year.
It's auth-svc now, our own service.
One, the app asks for its orders with the access token.
Two, the gateway comes back with a 401, token expired. Replies are dashed.
That one should land on the app, there.
Three, the app posts its refresh token to, um, the gateway?
No, I'm pretty sure slash token isn't behind the gateway, the app goes straight to auth-svc for that.
Squeezing auth over so Redis fits, that's where the refresh tokens live.
Four, auth-svc looks the refresh token up and rotates it, so the old one is dead after this.
Five, the new tokens go back to the app.
Well, not from Redis, that's wrong, Redis never talks to the app.
And six, the app retries the original request with the new access token.

add.text:
loop: refresh retried up to 3x
backoff 1s, 2s, 4s, then log out

steps.say: This box is a loop, if the refresh itself fails with a 5xx it tries again, three times I think, and then it logs the driver out.

steps.note: not sure what happens to other requests in flight while it refreshes, do they all try to refresh at once?

steps.say: That last part I genuinely don't know, and with rotation it might matter.

final_labels:
loop: refresh retried up to 3x
backoff 1s, 2s, 4s, then log out
story: the four tall boxes are lifelines (Driver app (iOS), API gateway, auth-svc, Redis) and time runs down the page; the numbers 1-6 on the arrows are the order

1 the app calls GET /orders, 2 the gateway replies 401 token_expired, 3 the app posts the refresh token, 4 auth-svc checks and rotates it in Redis, 5 auth-svc returns new access + refresh tokens, 6 the app retries GET /orders
step 3 first went to the API gateway; he changed his mind: /token is not behind the gateway, the app calls auth-svc directly (he is 'pretty sure')
step 5 was first drawn from Redis to the app and deleted, because Redis never talks to the app; the new tokens come from auth-svc
auth-svc was labelled 'Auth0?' at first; they moved off Auth0 last year and it is their own service now
refresh tokens are rotated: after step 4 the old refresh token no longer works
the hand-drawn box around steps 3-5 is a loop: if the refresh fails with a 5xx it is retried up to 3 times with backoff 1s, 2s, 4s, then the driver is logged out (he thinks three times)
he does not know what other in-flight requests do while a refresh is happening, and suspects it matters because of rotation
partner_should_ask_about: when several requests get a 401 at once, does each one refresh, and what happens to the second refresh once the first has rotated the token?
is the retry loop only for 5xx, or does a 4xx from the refresh (token already rotated) go straight to logout?
is he sure /token/refresh bypasses the gateway (he was unsure and switched it)
